title: Asset Inventory — User Manual
summary: How to add, find, check out, and report on assets in the Asset Inventory.

sections.body:
Overview

Asset Inventory is the central register of every physical/IT asset the organization tracks — laptops, AV gear, networking equipment, and more. Each asset belongs to a category, and categories can define their own custom fields via Form Templates.

Key Features

  • Add Hardware Asset — create a single asset; the form adapts to the chosen category's custom fields.
  • Category filter chips across the top of the list for quick filtering.
  • QR codes: Scan QR Code to jump straight to an asset, and per-row Print QR label.
  • Discover Unregistered Assets — surfaces agent-reported or network-scanned devices not yet in the register.
  • Import CSV (column-mapping wizard) and Export CSV / Export JSON for bulk data movement.
  • Bulk row selection with an Apply Status action.

Asset Detail Page Tabs

Opening an asset shows an "Asset Explorer" sidebar with tabs that adapt to the asset's category. Always present: Asset Profile, Impact Analysis, Location History & Map, Management, Contracts, Documents, Reports, Logs. For computer/network-type categories, additional tabs appear: Operating systems, Components, Volumes, Software, Connections, Network Ports, Sockets, Remote management, Virtualization, Antiviruses.

Step-by-Step

  1. Click Add Hardware Asset, pick a category, and fill in the fields (including any custom fields defined for that category).
  2. To hand an asset to someone, open it, go to Asset Profile, and click Check Out — pick who it's going to ("Check Out To") and confirm.
  3. When it's returned, open the same asset and click Check In. The full history is kept under "Checkout History".
  4. To bulk-import, click Import CSV and map your spreadsheet's columns to asset fields.
  5. To find devices that exist on the network but aren't registered yet, click Discover Unregistered Assets.

Tips

  • Harness/rigging equipment lives in the separate Harness Register menu, not here — see that manual.
  • Deleting is permission-gated; most roles can only edit, not delete.
